title: Helping hand for Sunlu Filament Connector
description:
A helping hand to connect filaments with the Sunlu Filament Connector to ensure a good connection.

The Sunlu Filament Connector is a great device, but in case that the filament is under (a lot of) tension, you need an extra hand.

When there is tension in the filament, a specially if there is not much filament left on the spool, you need both hand to get the filament in a straight line and you need a third hand to close and open the lid.

I designed a clamp in which you can clamp and straighten one end of the filament. Slide the clamp in the baseplate and it aligns perfectly with the fusion part of the filament connector. Now you have 1 hand free to operate the filament connector.

Put the device fits in the baseplate with a light press and the power connector goes through the baseplate. The clamp can be use on the right or left side.

The clamps needs to be completed wit a M3 threaded insert and an M3 bolt of 10 mm. 

I used the screw knob from David_J:  https://www.printables.com/model/494255-m3-screw-knob

title: Honda Civic EG, Del Sol Front Lower Control Arm Bushings
description:
These are models of the two bushings on the front lower control arms of the (92-95) Honda Civic EG, (93-97) Del Sol. These are designed to use the stock metal sleeves from the old bushings (The part the bolts go through), so you'll have to get all the old rubber off those to use with these (Most people burn the rubber off with a torch to make it easy). I designed the inside of the bushing with little notches to hold silicone grease better and keep them from squeaking so lube the inside up before putting in the metal sleeve. 

NOTE: I highly recommend printing in TPU since bushings are usually made of urethane or rubber, I don't think plastic would hold up or be safe.

For when you need that little extra bit of reach to unhook the seatbelt. Thanks Nancy for helping us design this. :)

Hooks directly onto the seatbelt, no adhesive or hardware required. It should slide freely up and down the seatbelt. When attached to the seatbelt, the clips should be against the body, and the flat face should be facing away from the body. The part that opens the seatbelt is slightly angled in towards the user to make hitting the seatbelt button easier.

The original version had built in supports, which have been removed in this version for use with your slicing software of choice.

Feel free to mess around with infill/resolution or any other settings you want to mess with. This isn't a picky print, and it's pretty hard to mess up.

The model in the pictures is an older version. The only change I've made to it was to round off most of the corners to avoid snags on clothing, but other than that the design is the same.

Let me know if you have any questions!

title: BMW E46 non-M 38mm Fuel Pump Adapter
description:
A simple fuel pump mounting bracket for BMW E46 non M. It fits into the stock location perfectly and is sturdy. Fully allows you to keep the stock fuel pump assembly with an aftermarket high flow fuel pump.

This requires a hose clamp to hold the assembly together. Best to assemble it around the pump and then put it into the fuel pump hanger. A 2nd clamp on the bottom portion of the assembly is suggested but not required.

It is a split shell design to allow for inconsistencies in fuel pump diameter and better clamping force to hold it all together.

Print with POM (OEM material for stock E46 hanger), PP, or Nylon. 

PETG (to my limited knowledge) is only good for a short amount of time. Use as a test only.

DO NOT print with: ABS, ASA, PLA, or any of their derivatives.

If in doubt look up a datasheet on your chosen filament. Use logic when selecting one- using the wrong filament can and will cause damage to your fuel system or even engine.

Use of supports is required.

It took about 1.2hr to print on a Bambu Labs P1P with an enclosure. Use of an enclosure to print is suggested.

title: remix for filament runout sensor
description:
This is a suggested improvement for using 626 bearings for the original design located here:

https://www.thingiverse.com/thing:4937795

I had trouble getting the filament to trigger the old z height sensor I had laying around so I moved a few things around to get the filament to slide and activate the sensor. I had to do some light sanding to even up the edges and to ensure I could hear the switch click when moving the slider back and forth.

The slide has been shortened and narrowed and the bearing axle moved closer to the filament.

Also made room on the cover to accommodate changes to the slider.  All other parts should be sourced from the original design.

I also plan on using (hot-glue) a short spring from a pen to help ensure the slider opens the switch when the filament runs out.  This might not be necessary but I figured it shouldn't hurt as long as I can get everything closed up with the spring glued in place.

Threading filament can be challenging due to the tendency for filament to curve slightly.

NOTE: This design uses a 626 bearing but that size was not specified in the original design when I initially did the remix.

Beware that the spring might introduce too much friction if it's too strong

title: Emergency mask for hospital respirators
description:
Following some requests, we indicate recommended but not mandatory print settings for the 3D production of Charlotte and Dave components for the assisted breathing mask. For the production of these pieces, since high precision is not required, an FDM filament printer with "basic" settings is more than sufficient;

Filament: PLA 1.75 mm
Nozzle temperature: 205 - 210 ° C
Top temperature: 35 - 50 ° C
Layer thickness: 0.2 mm
Supports: only resting on the printing bed.

Orientation: Charlotte resting on the terminal plane (as in the images), Dave resting on the larger diameter vertically.

As for the printing material, we recommend the most common filament on the market, the PLA (polylactic); this for several reasons:

Odorless (remember that patients must breathe air passing through these components)
The least dangerous possible (PLA is not very dangerous and biocomposable)
Relatively flexible (it must be able to deform elastically to be able to couple with other components).

title: 5-32 Deck Gun - US Navy
description:
This is a model of a 5-32 deck gun based off of a Gearing Class Destroyer. It is a model, not a working thing, it will rotate around 360 degrees and the cannons will rotate up and down by turning the side slot in the drive shaft with a coin or screw driver. It does not fire projectiles. 

It comes in several pieces that you have to put together that can be secured with glue. There is an exploded drawing in the set of PDFs. It is a little tricky to assemble and line up the cannons.

The models were built 1:1, so the STL should be scaled equally to fit the printer used. Check the size of the STL when you first open them to see how big they import. The initial scale might fit your printer. If you scale, every piece will have to be the same.

The gun house has a break away piece on the back lower side (it is a light grey in the PDF). I had a terrible time removing support material from that area and making it look good. The support piece is approximately one printer layer level below the main structure so it should be removed with a thin screwdriver. It should pry right off. The base also has the breakaway piece (This also helps with post printing cleaning as support material can be difficult to remove). I uploaded different variations, you can pick whichever. The pieces with the "legs" sticking out are for a larger base/raft to get a good adhesion to the built plate. I printed in PLA w/o a heated built plate and could not get the thing to stick down. So I design these "raft legs" in the print, during/after the printing of the raft/legs, I would tape the outrigger pieces to the built plate to keep the raft/model from peeling up. I used Kapton tape. Post printing you should be able to pry the extra support material off and it should leave an reasonably smooth surface.

The Rotary Stop has to be placed in the front center of the house as a final step. Center it and glue it.

title: Türarretierung / Feststellwinkel für Weinsberg Pepper 600 MEG 2020
description:
Mit diesem Druck kann die Eingangstür vom Wohnmobil an die Seitentür vom Fiat befestigt werden. Somit wird die Tür auch bei Wind arretiert und schlägt nicht ungewollt zu - das Fliegengitter bleibt heile.
Dieser Druck ist ein Remix der Türarretierung vom 2018er Modell und nun an die speziellen Abmessungen vom 2020er Weinsberg Pepper 600 MEG angepasst.

Das Design ist in einer Gemeinschaftsarbeit von Mitgliedern der my-pepper.de Community entstanden und bietet mit dem optionalen Winkel einen zusätzlichen Halteschutz - Danke dir lieber Werner :-) 
Der Feststellwinkel kann, wie im Foto zu sehen ist, mit einer Schraube und einer Flügelmutter bombenfest montiert werden - die Arretierung kann aber auch ohne den Feststellwinkel genutzt werden.

Gedruckt habe ich mit PETG, 20% Füllung mit Stützstruktur - viel Spaß bei nachdrucken

Update: Nun auch eine Version vom Feststellwinkel mit 7mm Loch (falls kein Gewindeschneider zur Hand)

Update2: MichaelHK hatte sich ebenfalls an die Verbesserung/Optimierung gemacht und mir/uns die Variante zur Verfügung gestellt. Im Download mit dem vorgestellten Dateinamen MichaelHK_ zu erkennen und selbsterklärend zu verwenden.

Update3: Wird die Türarretierung nicht benötigt kann sie nun mit einer Halterung im Pepper hängend verstaut werden. Für den Druck liegen zwei Varianten bereit - Links- bzw.  Rechtanschlag. So kann die Halterung nach eigenen Wünschen platziert werden und die Türarretierung inkl. Feststellwinkel ist immer griffbereit.

Vielen Dank an die Community für die Community ;-)

title: M3 Lee [American Medium Tank] (w/ M3 Grant turret+sand shields)
description:
The M3 Lee, officially Medium Tank, M3, was an American medium tank built in the beginning of the 1940s. The British named it "Lee" after Confederate General Robert E. Lee. Although the gun performed well, the tank had many drawbacks, including a high silhouette and the main gun being mounted in a sponson. However, a good mass-produced tank was in demand to combat the Axis blitzkrieg, and thousands of M3s were exported to the United Kingdom and Soviet Union. The British named their tanks the "M3 Grant" after American General Ulysses S. Grant to differentiate their tanks from the M3 Lee. The Grant received a new turret that got rid of the machine gun cupola. Most Grants also received sand shields for use in North Africa. After the Germans started mounting more powerful guns on their tanks, as well as the unusual design of the M3, the M3 was phased out by the new M4 Sherman. After that, the U.S. recalled the M3 Lee from the European theater. However, the British continued to use the M3 Grant against the Japanese up until 1945.

title: Laser beam aligner
description:
When you have aligned your lasers beampath to perfection, you now need to be sure the beam is 100% vertical to make a straight cut through the material.
Here you have a simple tool to make this alignment. 

-First make sure you hit the nozzle in the middle by adjusting your mirrors.
 (for this I use a homemade gauge with some painters tape)
-Put a piece of painters tape under the cone.
-Place the cone directly under the nozzle and raise the table until the cone centers gently on the tip.
-Fire a short pulse. 
-Now it's easy to see if the spot is in center using the aiming lines under the cone. 

If not, you need to move the cutting head a little bit, and then try again until you hit dead center. 
(Remember to check and adjust also at the nozzle every time you move the head)

-PEPSI-

title: How to run Customizer on your own computer
description:
**This page won't be updated anymore. [The new page with more up-to-date instructions is now here.](https://www.dr-lex.be/3d-printing/customizer.html)**

Please do not ask questions in this thing's comments about how to fix a problem with Customizer on Thingiverse. The whole purpose of these instructions, is to tell you how to run Customizer without needing the Thingiverse website at all.

*Old description below.*

This is a useless customizable thing, to demonstrate how to create a customized STL on your own computer instead of having to rely on Thingiverse's on-line Customizer app which has a history of breaking at random moments, sometimes for extended periods. For instance at the moment when I created this, attempting to run Customizer on the website resulted in this error at the side of the Thingiverse server:
*“/usr/local/bin/openscad/openscad: error while loading shared libraries: libCGAL.so.10: cannot open shared object file: No such file or directory”*

Another advantage of running Customizer locally even if the on-line one works fine, is that you do not need to wait for your turn in the processing queue. Moreover, you have a much better and faster preview of the model, which you can rotate and zoom freely. And last but not least, you have better control over the parameters.

In a nutshell, the **steps** to run Customizer on your own computer are (see images for steps 4 to 8):
1. Download and install OpenSCAD. You need [version 2019.05 or newer](https://www.openscad.org/downloads.html) to be able to use the customizer feature and for the following instructions to work. You can also use the latest development snapshot if you wish (this one has a blue icon instead of the usual yellow program icon).
2. Download the *.scad* file of the Thing you want to customize. If it also has a *.json* file, you can download this as well and place it next to the .scad file, but it is not essential. Then open the .scad file in OpenSCAD.
3. (Ignore this step, it was only applicable to previous versions.)
4. Make sure ‘Hide Customizer’ is not checked in the View menu. The Customizer UI should be visible at the right.
5. Hit the Preview button (F5) to enable the customizer interface (this makes no sense but the ritual in previous versions was even worse). Click the triangle icons to expand controls for their sections. Now you should be able to edit the values as you would in the online Customizer.
6. If ‘Automatic preview’ is not enabled, hit the Preview button (F5) again to get a quick preview of your current settings. You may need to press enter after editing values in edit fields to view the effect.
7. When ready, hit the Render button (F6). This may take a while.
8. When the model has been rendered, click the STL button to export the custom STL file.
9. If you want to save your current settings, click the ‘+’ button. To update the currently selected preset, click ‘Save preset’.

There are some **limitations** compared to the Thingiverse customizer. For instance drawing a shape ([like here](https://www.thingiverse.com/thing:270289)) is not yet implemented in OpenSCAD at the time of this writing, you can only enter raw coordinates. There is also a problem with customizers that use an image as input to generate a shape, like lithophanes: if you use a PNG or JPG image, the shape will be too tall by a factor 100. You can fix this by changing the appropriate scaling factor in the source code, an example can be found in the comments.

Obviously **this only works for Things that have been designed to be customizable.** If there is no *‘Open in Customizer’* button on the Thing page, you cannot magically make it customizable. (Only if a thing has a .scad file, it is possible to make it Customizer-friendly but this requires basic knowledge of OpenSCAD. [Here](http://customizer.makerbot.com/docs) is some basic documentation about converting a scad file to make it customizable.)

Some customizable things rely on OpenSCAD **libraries** that aren't installed. In that case you will get errors like: *“Can't open library '…'”.* You will need to find where you can download the library (e.g. ‘write’ can be found [here](https://www.thingiverse.com/thing:16193)), and place it inside the same folder as the .scad file.

The same goes for other dependencies like **fonts.** If you try to use a font that is not on your computer, a boring default font will be used instead. If you want to use any of the fonts that were available in the Thingiverse customizer, you will have to search for them on the web and install them on your own computer. You can of course also edit the name of the font in the source code of the .scad file, and use any font you already have on your system.
 

**A bit of extra info:**
Customizer is based on [OpenSCAD](http://www.openscad.org/), a program that can generate 3D models out of a set of instructions. A customizer file is just a .scad file with specific formatting. You can use any version of OpenSCAD to load and edit a customizer file, but I highly recommend using version 2019.05 or newer. You can also use the latest [development snapshot](http://www.openscad.org/downloads.html#snapshots) to get the latest bells and whistles (and bugs).

The customizer inside OpenSCAD has a *presets* feature. Presets are saved to a .json file with the same name as the .scad file. If you want to distribute presets with your Thing, also upload the JSON file to Thingiverse. (Keep in mind that these presets only work in OpenSCAD, they are not available in the online Customizer.)

OpenSCAD has two modes: a fast preview mode (F5 key), and a (usually slow) render mode which produces a model that can be saved for printing (F6 key). Tweak the customizer parameters in preview mode, and only render when satisfied with the preview, because rendering can take long depending on how complex the model is. Finally, you must export the model to an STL file which you can then print like any other file you would have downloaded.
 

*Notice to Thingiverse: please don't use this as an excuse to postpone fixing the online customizer!*

title: Lasercut: Manta-ray 3D puzzle
description:
This time, I'd like to introduce the "manta ray" 3D puzzle, created using a laser cutter and MDF material. This piece, inspired by the shape of a manta ray, features a simple yet dynamic design, making it a unique and captivating presence in any space.


#### Materials and Tools
The puzzle was crafted using 2.5mm thick MDF (medium-density fiberboard), cut with a laser cutter. MDF is an ideal material for creating puzzles and 3D structures as it is easy to work with and cuts cleanly with a laser.

I used a Etcher Laser Pro for this project. Its high precision made it easy to cut even the more complex design elements.


#### Design and Production Process
The manta ray design began as a 3D model, which was then transformed into a 2D slices. This method simplifies complex shapes into easily assembled parts, making the assembly process smooth and intuitive. The puzzle uses a slot-assembly system, so no glue is required, allowing the pieces to fit together like a puzzle.

Once the design was finalized, I converted it into a digital file compatible with the laser cutter, which then cut out the MDF pieces. By manually assembling the cut pieces, I brought the manta's sleek, grid-like form to life.


#### Finished Product
The completed "Manta ray," as shown in the image, boasts elegant curves and a beautiful lattice structure. The use of thick MDF ensures that the puzzle is sturdy and can double as a decorative piece or display object.


#### For Those Who Want to Try
This project is accessible even for beginners with a laser cutter and is perfect for anyone looking to create their own custom puzzle or art piece. Feel free to give it a try!

title: Wall-mounted microphone arm for the at2100
description:
This wall mounted microphone arm is designed to hold the at2100 usb / xlr microphone. I designed this because my current microphone arm was always pushing down on my desk too hard, and it was also just getting in the way. This was my first time designing anything with articulation so I did not include screws in the model, instead I just left holes for pre-made screws.The arm should be relatively easy to resize to fit different microphones. 

*Update*
After putting the model together, i realized there is not much support holding it up, so you only can use a few of the arm parts. In the future I'd like to make this design sturdier, so it can hold up the microphone further out.
(I'm holding it up in the picture because I haven't found a good spot to put it yet.)
_________________________________________________________________________
Building instructions

The Wall mount itself can screw to the wall, with the extruding part being on one of the sides. Then the first arm part is connected to the wall mount, using a screw through the hole on the extruding part. Then you just connect however many arm parts you need to reach where you are trying to. Once you reach where you need to, the microphone grip’s pole is inserted into one of the holes in the final arm part. The pole may require some minimal sanding to be able to fit into the arm part.

title: Micro RC Star Wars Mouse Droid - Remix
description:
Summary:

Remixed the Remix By kchristley (https://www.thingiverse.com/thing:2856616) of the awesome Mini Mouse droid by jedynak. I modified the model by kchristley to accept a newer version of the 1/58 scale RC Coke Can radio controlled car found on Amazon (https://a.co/d/0fzneG0D). I used JoyMonkey's Antenna Files (https://www.thingiverse.com/thing:1862673), I just scaled them down.

Just remove the screws, two from front and one from rear to be able to remove the cars cover and rear bumper.


Files:
Micro_Mouse_Top (61.8mm, 48.8mm, 38.7mm)
Micro_Mouse_Brim (73.5mm, 52.5mm, 6mm)
Micro_Mouse_Top_Greeblies_set (8.14mm, 33.0mm, .75mm)




Improvements:

1) The car fits in tight. One change I would suggest from my setup in the photos. Would be to loosen the rear leds from the car frame. This would allow the top shell to sit down into the brim better (level) and then the brim would sit on the screw hole for the bumper (leveling the whole print on the car).

2) If you could find the same rear red leds. Remove the front clear leds and replace with red ones. Then after mounting Greebles, drill two holes in front and back of the shell and through the greeble base. So, the leds could be placed in these holes. Have one front and one rear in the front holes and the same setup in the back shell holes. This way when driving forward or backwards there would be a red light on under the greebles, when driving in either direction.

title: Print2Play: Home Run Rally
description:
### Print2Play: Home Run Rally

---

#### Description:
Print2Play: Home Run Rally is a 3D-printed game inspired by the ancient game of Pachisi, which has since evolved into popular variations like Ludo and Mensch ärgere dich nicht. This version brings a classic board game experience to life, allowing players to enjoy multiple styles of gameplay.

The set includes files for the board, player pieces, and colored dice, with options to print dice in each color if desired. Alternatively, use your own dice or grab them from my "[Print2Play: All-Size Dice](https://www.thingiverse.com/thing:6775272)" project.

**Notes**: To check fit and compatibility, test files (test_board.stl and test_fields.stl) are included.

🎲 Looking for more games? Explore the full Print2Play collection and find even more exciting games and designs! [Print2Play Collection](https://www.thingiverse.com/print3dtv/collections/42667754/things)

🌟 Want to see all my 3D printed projects? Check out my latest designs here: [Print3Dtv Designs](https://www.thingiverse.com/print3dtv/designs)
Or explore specific collections like Print2Play, Everyday Essentials, and more: [Print3Dtv Collections](https://www.thingiverse.com/print3dtv/collections)

---

#### Files:
- **board.stl**: Main game board.
- **fields_pieces.stl**: Player pieces and fields.
- **fields_pieces_dice.stl**: Includes pieces, fields, and one die per player color.
- **white_fields.stl**: Neutral fields for the game board perimeter.
- **test_board.stl**: A small portion of the board for testing fit.
- **test_fields.stl**: Test piece for field fit.

---

#### Dimensions:
- **Length**: 250 mm
- **Width**: 250 mm
- **Height**: 3 mm

---

#### Printer and Print Settings:
- **Printer**: Artillery Sidewinder X2
- **Material**: PLA
- **Nozzle**: 0.6mm (Board) | 0.4mm (Remaining Components)
- **Profile**: 0.2mm layer height
- **Infill**: 20%
- **Print Speed**: 75mm/s (Board) | 60mm/s (Remaining Components)

---

#### Instructions:
1. Print test files to ensure fit.
2. Print the game board and all desired pieces.
3. Optional: Print separate dice for each color, or use from the "[Print2Play: All-Size Dice](https://www.thingiverse.com/thing:6775272)" project.

---

#### Video Links:
- [Timelapse & Presentation Video](https://youtu.be/DqWZag0kWk4): Watch the print process and final model showcase.

---

#### Feedback:
Your feedback is highly appreciated! Feel free to suggest enhancements, share your print, or leave positive feedback.

title: BOTW ancient Guardian for 3D print (tinkercad)
description:
I wanted to make a toy Guardian from The Legend Of Zelda: Breath Of The Wild after playing the game recently. I looked on thingiverse and did not find what I was looking for. So I found the best of various models and combined them through TinkerCAD. I did not actually cut bits and put them together, I made a rough copy out of TinkerCAD-based geometry. 

FEATURES
The head is designed to rotate, and the planetary gearbox in the lower/main body means the mid body will rotate in the opposite direction. The head was originally designed to have an LED in it, but I gave up on it. the space is still in the head, and I put a switch holder in as well. there is no eye, as it was supposed to use a blue LED. The switch is supposed to be the same kind used as 3D printer limit switches, but I can't find the proper name right now.
The switch is supposed to be activated by pulling up the head and twisting it over. 

I used acrylic paint for detail and 18 gauge steel floral wire to support the legs. I used superglue to attach all pieces.

NOTE
this is a difficult print. parts may fail.

UPDATE: re-uploaded the main body so hopefully it will print better. I have not tested this yet, so be warned.

I used needle-nosed pliers to loosen the gears and than added WD-40 for lubrication. two of six gears broke and were removed, but the print still worked. Legs were too long, and not flexible enough. I am working on a V2 as of 7/15/2024. Link to original TinkerCAD model: https://www.tinkercad.com/things/53S5f0eC3Xn-3d-print-botw-guardian-fully-printable

title: Club Ox Dancing Monster - Esso_Bregor
description:
This project is my attempt to create a toy for my grandson. It is modeled after video and photos of the Clubbox Earth Island Singing Monster. My focus was to design and 3D print the parts that give the Singing Monster it's identity and make those parts able to connect to the STEM toy ball/clip and clip/clip pieces that I have utilized as the neck, arms and legs. Springs can be added to the piston arms and to the back of the radio. If you are able to get a thin plastic mirror to place between the body back plate and the body. This will give the body a "See Through Effect". The pieces mentioned above allow the toy to be posed and to be more animated.

I am new to 3D design and printing. My designs are created on TinkerCAD and I use Lychee Slicer to prep for prints (Note: lift the objects at least 5mm when generating supports). My equipment is Elegoo Saturn 3 Resin Printer with12k resolution and I prefer to use Siraya Resins as is or mixed to create a more durable print. For this project I used a 50/50 mix of tough and flex resins which has a firm but slightly rubbery feel prior to curing. Remember that curing increases hardness.

title: JBL Flip 5 Holder / Wall Holder
description:
Moin Moin.

Dies ist ein Wandhalter für die JBL Flip 5/4, (Ich habe keine andere hier zum ausprobieren)
ich habe dieses Modell mit 3 Wänden Gedruckt, Können aber auch mehr sein zur Stabilität, der Infill muss dann gar nicht so hoch sein 10% reichen dann schon, die Bohrungen sind 4mm groß Können aber zur Not aufgebohrt werden ist dann aber blöd mit den Senkungen.
Die Boxen werden bei mir ohne Probleme oder wackeln von M4x20mm Schrauben gehalten.

Viel Spaß beim Drucken, Verbesserungsvorschläge werden Gerne angenommen ;)  

PS: Muss flach aufs Druckbett Platziert werden, (Also mit dem Boden Flach auf das Druckbett)




This is a wall mount for the JBL Flip 5/4, (I don't have any others here to try)
I printed this model with 3 walls, but it can also be more for stability, the infill doesn't have to be that high, 10% is enough, the holes are 4mm large, but it can be drilled out if necessary, but then it's stupid with the countersinks.
The boxes are held in place by M4x20mm screws without any problems or wobbling.

Have fun printing, suggestions for improvements are welcome ;) 


PS: Must be placed flat on the print bed (i.e. with the bottom flat on the print bed)

title: The SK Filament Dry Box
description:
I have printed and configured over 10 variations of a dry box and the photo above is my final concoction. I call it a concoction because i took parts from multiple filament boxes posted and used them in one project along with some modding some of the pieces to make it to my liking. 

THINGS YOU WILL NEED
- 18Qt Waterproof Storage Tote
https://www.homedepot.com/p/Ezy-Storage-18L-19Qt-Waterproof-Clear-Latch-Tote-IP-67-FBA34060/314650516

- 5/16 Threaded Rod 
https://www.homedepot.com/p/Everbilt-5-16-in-x-36-in-Zinc-Plated-Fine-Threaded-Rod-800807/204325651

- (12) 5/16 nuts
https://www.homedepot.com/p/Everbilt-5-16-in-18-Zinc-Plated-Hex-Nut-801746/204647888

- Small drill bit
(exact size coming soon)

- Something To Cut Threaded Rod

- (6) 608 Bearings 
https://www.amazon.com/gp/product/B08KT5TF6Z/ref=ppx_yo_dt_b_search_asin_title?ie=UTF8&psc=1

- Bowden Tubing and Fittings
https://www.amazon.com/gp/product/B08FYS797F/ref=ppx_yo_dt_b_asin_title_o00_s00?ie=UTF8&th=1
(You will be using the PC4-M10 Black End fittings)

- Mini Hygrometer Thermometer
https://www.amazon.com/gp/product/B07QC7JRDP/ref=ppx_yo_dt_b_asin_title_o08_s00?ie=UTF8&psc=1

(6) Small screws with washers and nuts for filament guide
(exact size coming soon)

(4) Small screws with washers and nuts for rod holder
(exact size coming soon)


Alright, let's get this party started.

After acquiring everything above, we need to start printing parts. Let's start with the rollers. StvPtrsn designed amazing rollers. We are going use his design but change how we use them. StvPtrsn uses his for the edges of the spools to roll on. I found using his rollers though the middle of the spool is best. This way you don't have to worry about a damaged spool slipping or falling off track. I print at 150mm/s and the filament rolls off them effortlessly and never pull more filament then needed. I go close up in the YouTube video posted below of how well the filament rolls off the spool. 
Here is a link to StvPtrsn's rollers below.
https://www.thingiverse.com/thing:3947469
Go ahead and print (6) "Spool_Roller_75mm" and (1) "Rod Holder"

Now print my two modded items in this post. (1) "Rod End Open Holder" and (2) "Rod Holder End Cap"

You now have all the parts you need for the rollers.

Now let's print the parts we need for the Filament Guides.
Bradcfisher did an outstanding job with his and that's what we are going to use. 
Here is his link:
https://www.thingiverse.com/thing:2896547
Print (3) "12mm_x_42mm_bolt_1.75mm_filament_PC4-M10_fitting"
(3) "12mm_nut"
(3) "frame_inner"
(3) "frame_outer"

I have an Ender 3 S1 Pro. When i removed my stock filament spool holder, it had the filament sensor mount attached. I had to print a new one for my setup. I modded a part at the time but can not find the file. Joaolsneto designed one that looks like it should work.
Here is his link:
https://www.thingiverse.com/thing:5332875?fbclid=IwAR2p9hbgZThSzyedy5eBuVJIjNCNa2qOyNbalYFWkq5at6fywNLOsaRhHr0

Let's finish up by printing the humidity sensor holder.
Dstarke designed an awesome holder for our sensor.
Here is his link:
https://www.thingiverse.com/thing:5262772


You now have all the pieces needed to assemble The SK Filament Dry Box.
Below is a YouTube video showing you how to assemble.
VIDEO COMING SOON!

Enjoy!

NOTE: Some may say it is not a "true dry box" without a heating element and that may be true. I consider the silica gel packs i drop in the tote "drying" out the filament. My setup currently does not have one. My box stays at 30-32 percent humidity and I live in Michigan in the United States of America. Would a heating element help? Probably. Do i currently feel my setup needs one? No, i do not. That may not be the same for you. If i ever were to add one, I would go with something like this.
https://www.amazon.com/dp/B08XWQQNG5/ref=twister_B0C4BGV7S1?_encoding=UTF8&th=1

===============================================================================================================

					──What is the HOLSTER and Why?──                                                                                                                         
	With the rise of decent-enough hand tracking and multimodal features on the Quest Pro and Quest 3, I found 
myself wanting to use hand tracking as much as possible. After a small acclimation period, hand tracking has become my 
preferred method of basic navigation. However, I still strongly believe that tracked controllers within 
Virtual Reality can be a powerful tool - just that they don't have to be (and perhaps shouldn't be) the default method 
to interact with virtual interfaces. 

There are a few problems I ran into, though! 

Every time I transition from hand tracking to controller usage, there is a small window of time where I have to 
look around my playspace to find my controllers. This feeling is reminiscent of "losing the remote" to the TV.
In essence, not a good feeling. The inverse situation is just as anxiety-inducing - transitioning back 
to hand tracking and carefully placing my controllers in a spot that is "out of sight enough" so that the 
headset properly transitions to hand tracking, but in a memorable spot so that I can easily find them when 
prompted again. Somehow, in the disorientation of leaving Virtual Reality, I seem to always forget that 
memorable spot. 

I imagined how this entire situation could potentially be better - How can we completely cut out this little
slice of anxiety and friction? Enter, ─HOLSTER─. The idea is simple: if the controller is a tool, why not 
have a method of keeping the tool easily accessible at any time? Holster is exactly what it sounds like, a holster for
your tool (controllers) that keeps them readily available. 

But it actually goes even further than this!
In using Holster, I realized just how powerful multimodal (the ability to use hand tracking and controllers 
simultaneously) and the combination of having controllers at your hip can be - it's simply not being taken advantage of. 
With HOLSTER + multimodal, new gameplay potentials open up that were never possible before. I will potentially
be exploring some of these possibilities either in upcoming videos or within my Discord/Patreon. 

I strongly believe that something like Holster can make hand tracking and controller usage better, and I also believe
that something *like* Holster should be included in the box. Maybe through iteration and the power of
community, we can help make that abundantly clear. 

===============================================================================================================
USAGE RECOMMENDATIONS:

-Wear either pants or some clothing that has a place to "clip" in
-Jean pockets seem to be the best solution

-QUEST OS:
-If you are having issues with the controllers constantly popping up while using hand tracking,
you can turn off "automatic hand tracking- controller switching"
	You will then bump the controllers together to switch.

The automatic switching between tracking states will continue to be a slight issue depending on the 
environment until Meta creates a more robust method to handle multimodal actions at the OS level. 

===============================================================================================================

PRINT SETTINGS:

- Place the STL within your Slicer. 
- Print in the orientation that the model is set by default (ensures the clip is printed properly).
- Do not change scale.
- Duplicate and mirror to have both sides of the HOLSTER.
- You can print in either FDM or Resin, I personally chose Resin.

**STANDARD FDM:**
- 0.2mm layer height
- 30% infill
- Supports + Brim Enabled (Auto Support)

**RESIN PRINT:**
- Supports optional depending on Printer
- Put STL in Slicer; your settings depend on resin type.
- I personally had the best results with ANYCUBIC High Clear UV Resin.

title: Single Lane Slot Car Track
description:
You are looking at a single track system I am currently developing.
For test/rally/drag strip/hill climb track, you name it!

This is essentially a sample for people to test, I will later on expand more track pieces if this becomes popular and this could become an open-source track system for everybody to enjoy!

Easy to print, braid and assemble. All track pieces will fit on small size 3D printers (220 x 220).
Track is wide enough to not need any extra border pieces and potentially wide enough for small 1/24 cars like the Shelby Cobra in one of the pictures.

Tracks are 153 mm wide, 7.6 mm deep slot, 6.5 mm track braid wide.

I would advise to lay a single strip of track-braid once you've committed to a layout.
Alternatively, you could do as I did by making brass 'jumpers' or 'tabs' and secure them in place (2 mm holes present), just as showing on last picture. 

Note: Some of the pieces will get updated along the way, but the old ones will be compatible with new ones.

Johnny's Workshop
